title: Animal Behaviour and Migration
notes: **Reflex action:** involuntary, rapid, stereotyped response to stimulus. Pathway: receptor â†’ sensory neuron â†’ integration centre (spinal cord) â†’ motor neuron â†’ effector. Examples: knee jerk, withdrawal from pain.
**Taxes:** oriented movement toward (positive) or away from (negative) a stimulus. Phototaxis (light), chemotaxis (chemicals), geotaxis (gravity). Euglena shows positive phototaxis.
**Dominance and leadership:** social animals establish hierarchies. Dominant individuals get priority access to food and mates. Leaders guide group movement, often based on experience.
**Fish migration:** anadromous (sea to fresh water to breed: salmon), catadromous (fresh water to sea to breed: eel). Cues: temperature, day length, magnetic field, pheromones.

**Bird migration:** seasonal movement between breeding and wintering grounds. Cues: photoperiod, temperature, food availability. Navigate using stars, sun, magnetic field, landmarks. Examples: Arctic tern (longest migration), Siberian crane.
